result.summary: Our patch replaces the weak `startsWith(folder)` prefix test in DirectoryTraversal with a segment-boundary `isWithin` check, closing the sibling-directory-prefix bypass (e.g. "base" vs "base_secret") on both the external and classpath guards, and the external POV no longer reproduces with regressions passing. However, it does not perform true filesystem canonicalization (no getCanonicalPath / symlink resolution) and relies on upstream string-based cleanPath to have already resolved `../`, so it is a string-comparison hardening rather than the CWE-022 defense-of-record. It also diverges entirely from the official fix, which added path validation (WEB-INF/META-INF/file:/`../`) in ClassPathResource and does not touch the external route our patch strengthens.
result.root_cause: A weak prefix-based containment check for static-file paths that fails to enforce a path-segment boundary and does not canonicalize the resolved path (including symlinks) against the configured base directory before serving.

issues.description: No filesystem canonicalization or symlink resolution (uses toAbsolutePath and string startsWith, not getCanonicalPath/toRealPath). A symlink inside the configured folder pointing outside it could still escape the base directory.

Does not cover the classpath-resource validation the official fix adds in ClassPathResource (WEB-INF/META-INF/file:/`../` rejection). The classpath route protections remain weaker than the reference fix, and the two patches touch disjoint files (jaccard 0).

External check depends on upstream StringUtils.cleanPath to have resolved `../` before the guard; toAbsolutePath() alone does not normalize, so correctness against dot-segment payloads is implicit rather than enforced at the guard.
